activity.notes: Boran (Bōrān; also Buran, Puran and Burandukht in modern catalogues) was a daughter of Khosrow II and a ruling queen of the Sasanian Empire. Encyclopaedia Iranica places her accession in spring 630 after the death of Shahrvaraz and notes differing traditions for the length of her reign; it considers her probable death to have occurred in autumn 631, while extant coins are dated to the first, second and third regnal years. The British Museum independently catalogues Boran as a Sasanian ruler who ruled in 630-631. ATLAS therefore records one continuous 630-631 reign at year granularity: the 630 start year is treated as established, while the 631 end is marked approximate because the precise duration and terminal date remain debated. This Activity does not create a separate second reign or extend the reign to 632 without stronger evidence.

sources.title: Boran — Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.citation_text: Encyclopaedia Iranica identifies Boran as a Sasanian queen and daughter of Khosrow II, places her accession in spring 630, records competing reign-length traditions, and considers a death in autumn 631 probable.

sources.title: Boran — British Museum Collections Online
sources.citation_text: The British Museum catalogues Boran as a Persian ruler of the Sasanian Dynasty, daughter of Khusrau II, with ruled dates 630-631; it also records the variant names Burandukht, Buran and Puran.

sources.title: History and Coinage of the Sasanian Queen Boran (AD 629-631)
sources.citation_text: Hodge Mehdi Malek and Vesta Sarkhosh Curtis, The Numismatic Chronicle 158 (1998), pp. 113-129, is a dedicated scholarly study of Boran's history and coinage and dates the reign within the late 629-631 chronological framework.

sources.title: Women i. In Pre-Islamic Persia — Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.citation_text: Encyclopaedia Iranica identifies Boran as the reigning Sasanian queen of 630-31 and notes that her appearance on royal coinage was exceptional among Sasanian women.
